bull.argument: Costco's 2026 filing shows a business compounding on its core strengths. Net sales rose 10% to $297,247 million, comparable sales grew 8%, and net income climbed 14% to $9,226 million, or $20.76 per diluted share. Growth was broad: core merchandise categories rose in every category, and digitally-enabled comparable sales jumped 21%. Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907 million, and renewal rates held at 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada. The balance sheet is strong, with operating cash flow of $15,817 million, up from $13,335 million, and cash and short-term investments of $21,301 million. Management also raised the quarterly dividend 13% and plans roughly $7,500 million of capital spending with up to 33 new warehouses in 2027, signaling confidence in future demand. The filing does flag real risks, including concentration in California and Canada and tariff exposure. But the company has returned strong results despite these pressures, and its recurring membership model and self-funded growth support a favorable long-term case.

claims.claim: Net sales grew 10% in 2026, with comparable sales up 8%.
claims.quote: Net sales increased 10% to $297,247, driven by an increase in comparable sales and sales at new warehouses

claims.claim: Membership fee revenue rose 11%, supporting recurring income.
claims.quote: Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907, driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases, and upgrades to Executive membership

claims.claim: Operating cash flow strengthened and funds planned growth.
claims.quote: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $15,817 in 2026, compared to $13,335 in 2025

bear.argument: The opponent's case rests on headline growth, but the filing shows how concentrated and fragile that growth is. The U.S. and Canada supply 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income, and California alone is 26% of U.S. net sales, so a slowdown in one state could materially hit results. Growth is also leaning on items that are not core retail strength: gasoline prices added $3,501 million to net sales, and the filing says rising gasoline prices hurt gross margin percentage. Core merchandise gross margin fell 11 basis points on a stand-alone basis of the total, and the company says its low margins mean modest cost changes can swing net income. Tariff refunds of $184 million were one-time and partly reinvested in member prices, so they are not a durable earnings base. Meanwhile, capital spending is rising to about $7,500 million, and management says its plans may change. The stock price, the filing warns, already reflects high expectations, so any miss could push it down.

claims.claim: Heavy concentration in U.S. and Canadian operations and in California creates single-market risk.
claims.quote: Within the U.S., we are highly dependent on our California operations, which comprised 26% of U.S. net sales in 2026.

claims.claim: Gasoline price inflation materially boosted net sales and pressures gross margin percentage.
claims.quote: Higher gasoline prices positively impacted net sales by $3,501, or 130 basis points

claims.claim: The stock price already reflects high expectations, so any shortfall could cause a decline.
claims.quote: We believe that the price of our stock currently reflects high market expectations for our future operating results.

bull.argument: The opponent's concentration point is real, and the filing discloses it, but the same data shows broad strength. U.S. comparable sales rose 8%, and California is 26% of U.S. net sales within a business that grew across regions. On gasoline, the filing says excluding gasoline price inflation, gross margin percentage rose 10 basis points. The 11-basis-point core merchandise decline is largely a mix shift toward ancillary businesses, while core merchandise margin as a percentage of its own sales rose 15 basis points. The tariff refunds are small, $184 million, and not the thesis. Capex of about $7,500 million is expected to be funded from operations and existing cash, which stood at $21,301 million. The stock-expectations warning is a standard risk factor, but earnings grew 14% and the dividend rose 13%. The bull case rests on a recurring membership base, with 92.3% renewal in the U.S. and Canada, and on growth funded from internal cash.

claims.claim: Excluding gasoline inflation, gross margin percentage actually rose 10 basis points.
claims.quote: Excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points.

claims.claim: Core merchandise margin as a share of its own sales improved, so the decline reflects mix rather than weaker pricing power.
claims.quote: The gross margin in core merchandise categories when expressed as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points.

claims.claim: Membership renewal remains high, supporting the recurring income base; planned capex is expected to be funded internally.
claims.quote: These expenditures are expected to be financed with cash from operations, cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments.

bear.argument: The opponent says the concentration risk is disclosed but offset by broad strength, yet the filing's own numbers show the offset is narrower than presented. Excluding gasoline inflation, U.S. comparable sales growth was 7% and total company comparable growth was 7%, versus 8% reported, so much of the headline acceleration came from fuel. The 10 basis point gross margin improvement is also an ex-gasoline figure; reported gross margin percentage fell three basis points, and the filing says rising gasoline prices negatively impact gross margin percentage. The 15 basis point gain in core merchandise margin is measured on its own sales, while total core gross margin fell 11 basis points on the reported base. Mix is shifting toward lower-margin businesses, and the filing says digitally-enabled sales often carry lower margins. Cash of $21,301 million is real, but the filing shows capex rising to about $7,500 million with plans that may change. Strong renewal rates are reported for the U.S. and Canada only; worldwide renewal was 89.8%.

claims.claim: Reported gross margin percentage declined, and the filing ties gasoline price increases to lower gross margin percentage.
claims.quote: Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points; it increased 10 basis points excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation

claims.claim: Worldwide renewal is lower than the U.S. and Canada figure the opponent cited.
claims.quote: At the end of 2026, member renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide.

claims.claim: Capital plans are subject to change, so the spending outlook carries uncertainty.
claims.quote: There can be no assurance that current expectations will be realized, and plans are subject to change

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes from the filing, so evidence is strong on each side. The bear effectively rebutted the bull's gross margin and renewal framing by showing the 10 bp and 92.3% figures are ex-gasoline or U.S./Canada-only, which undercuts the bull's selective presentation. The bull's rebuttal on mix shift and funded capex is reasonable but leaves the reported margin decline and worldwide renewal point largely unanswered, so the debate is roughly even.
